question.problem: A function $f(x)=4x-\frac{6}{x}$ is defined on an interval $[a,6]$, where $a$ is a negative parameter. Calculate $a$ such that the average rate of  change over $[a,6]$ is equal to $3.$
question.worked_solution:
Let's calculate the average rate of change of $f(x)$ over the interval $[a,6]$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{Δf}{Δx} & =\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a} \\  & =\frac{(4(6)-\frac{6}{6})-(4(a)-\frac{6}{a})}{6-a} \\  & =\frac{23-4a+\frac{6}{a}}{6-a} \\  & =\frac{23-4a+\frac{6}{a}}{6-a}\cdot \frac{a}{a} \\  & =\frac{23a-4{a}^{2}+6}{a(6-a)} \\  & =\frac{6+23a-4{a}^{2}}{a(6-a)} \\  & =\frac{(6-a)(1+4a)}{a(6-a)} \\  & =\frac{\cancel{(6-a)}(1+4a)}{a\cancel{(6-a)}} \\  & =\frac{1+4a}{a}\end{aligned}
$$

We want $\frac{Δf}{Δx}$ be equal to $3$, so 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+4a}{a} & =3 \\ 1+4a & =3a \\ a & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $a<0$, we conclude that $a=-1$ and the interval is $[-1,6].$
